label: caiso 87 surplus clean
definition: KEEPER (promoted 2026-07-16, owner sign-off) caiso-87 surplus-clean import depth: the caiso-84 keeper recipe + caiso_dsw_surplus_clean=True — the measured WEIM surplus-hour clean import depth on the Palo Verde/Path-46 corridor (p95 depth-in-surplus 5,312/4,792/5,472 MW, CV 0.056, LOYO <=12.5%; EF 0, priced at the measured hub + wheel; trigger = measured PV hub below its own gas-coupled remote-CCGT floor, measured hours only; FINDING-caiso82 par.3 clean-DEPTH lane, FINDING-caiso86b closed the ladder-PRICE alternative). C3a +11.9/+12.6/+19.3% -> +10.3/+11.1/+16.6%; May-2023 gap +14.0 -> +11.7 (carbon rungs collapse out of surplus hours, DSW_CCGT May dispatch 725->93 MW); C1-2024 CC +6.67 -> +6.01 TWh; C3b-2025 NRMSE 0.220 -> 0.200 (at tolerance edge); C2-2025 gas -2.3%; C3c/C7/C8 unchanged as pre-registered. Remaining soft-month residual is the NORTH corridor's 1.8 GW PNW_midC truncation (marginal 35% of May hours post-fix) — its own charter. 2023-2025.
market_story: Imports: in surplus-West hours (measured Palo Verde hub below its own gas-coupled remote-CCGT floor — gas is not the hub's marginal resource) the real marginal import into CAISO is a WEIM/EDAM transfer attributed to CLEAN surplus resources under CARB's EIM GHG accounting, so it carries no unspecified border-carbon wedge; the measured CAISO-hub spread in those hours sits at parity. The model's clean depth previously truncated at the firm RA blocks + PNW_midC, mispricing surplus-hour imports at fossil CARB rungs (+$12-18). The keeper carries the measured year-stable depth-in-surplus on the south corridor at hub parity (EF 0), with fossil rungs pricing only the flow beyond it (secondary dispatch) — so soft-month middays/overnights clear at import parity as reality does, while non-surplus hours keep the full carbon ladder. Gas CC: cheaper surplus-hour imports displace part of the 2024 CC over-run (C1 +6.67 -> +6.01 TWh) without touching the winter gas-level mechanism (caiso-84, Jan/Feb-2023 unchanged).
